text: Asahna Bucha 2005: Thai Wikipedia's table says 20 July, my wan-phra says 21 July, and it is the only row before 2024 where we part. Which day did the temples keep?

The Thai full moon comes on average 0.9 h after the holy day ends, and the new moon 6.6 h into day 1. If day 1 is counted from the day the moon is new, the fifteenth lunar day ends at the full moon. Is that how the Thai reckoning means it? Find a Thai or Indian source that says what waxing 15 is for.

The Royal Institute paper counts 34 of 52 holy days off in B.E. 2557, but 2014 has 49 holy days on every list I can find. Where do 52 come from? Their full table, if the printed article has one, would show it, and which moment of the day they read the Moon at.
